```{r setup, include=FALSE}

#Load the Data
library(datasets)
library(rstatix)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

```{r}
# Calculate means for each stat by year
year_means <- games_all %>%
  group_by(Year) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_winning_score = mean(Winning.Score, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_losing_score  = mean(Losing.Score, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_total_score   = mean(Total.Score, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_margin = mean(Margin, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

year_means

```

```{r}
#Summary Stats All
summary_stats_all <- games_all |>
  group_by(Year) |>
  summarise(
    mean_winning_score = mean(Winning.Score),
    sd_winning_score = sd(Winning.Score),
    mean_losing_score = mean(Losing.Score),
    sd_losing_score = sd(Losing.Score),
    mean_total_score = mean(Total.Score),
    sd_total_score = sd(Total.Score),
    mean_margin = mean(Margin)
  )
```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(summary_stats_all, aes(x = factor(Year), y = mean_total_score)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean_total_score - sd_total_score,
                    ymax = mean_total_score + sd_total_score),
                width = 0.2, color = "black") +
  labs(title = "Average Total Score by Year",
       x = "Year", y = "Mean Total Score ± SD") +
  theme_minimal()


library(tidyr)

library(tidyr)

summary_long <- summary_stats_all |>
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("mean_"),
               names_to = "Metric", values_to = "Mean")

ggplot(summary_long |> filter(Metric %in% c("mean_winning_score", "mean_losing_score")),
       aes(x = Year, y = Mean, color = Metric)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  labs(title = "Average Winning vs Losing Scores by Year",
       x = "Year", y = "Mean Score", color = "Metric") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("mean_winning_score" = "darkgreen",
                                "mean_losing_score" = "red"),
                     labels = c("Winning Score", "Losing Score")) +
  theme_minimal()


ggplot(summary_stats_all, aes(x = Year, y = mean_margin)) +
  geom_line(color = "purple", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = "purple") +
  labs(title = "Average Margin of Victory by Year",
       x = "Year", y = "Mean Margin") +
  theme_minimal()

```


```{r}
anova_result <- games_all |>
  anova_test(Total.Score ~ Year)

print(anova_result)
summary(anova_result)
```
```{r}
#Pairwise Comparisons without Adjustment

pairwise_results <- games_all |>
  pairwise_t_test(Total.Score ~ Year, p.adjust.method = "none")

print(pairwise_results)
```

```{r}
# Pairwise Comparisons with Adjustments

#Bonferroni Correction
pairwise_results_bonf <- games_all |>
  pairwise_t_test(Total.Score ~ Year, p.adjust.method = "bonferroni")

print(pairwise_results_bonf)
pairwise_results_bonf <- pairwise_results_bonf |> rename(BONF_p.adj = p.adj)

#Holm Correction
pairwise_results_holm <- games_all |>
  pairwise_t_test(Total.Score ~ Year, p.adjust.method = "holm")

print(pairwise_results_holm)
pairwise_results_holm <- pairwise_results_holm |> rename(HOLM_p.adj = p.adj)

#False Discovery Rate (Benjamini-Hochberg)
pairwise_results_fdr <- games_all |>
  pairwise_t_test(Total.Score ~ Year, p.adjust.method = "fdr")

print(pairwise_results_fdr)


pairwise_results_fdr <- pairwise_results_fdr |> rename(FDR_p.adj = p.adj)

#Without adjustment, we are more likely to find significant differences, but we risk false positives (Type I errors).
#Bonferroni is very strict, reducing the likelihood of false positives but possibly missing real differences (false negatives).
#Holm correction provides a balance, still controlling Type I errors but retaining more statistical power.
#Benjamini-Hochberg correction allows for more discoveries, making it useful when multiple comparisons are needed, but it comes with a slightly increased risk of false positives.
```


```{r}
# Summary Table
comparison_table <-  
bind_cols(pairwise_results,pairwise_results_bonf$BONF_p.adj, pairwise_results_holm$HOLM_p.adj,pairwise_results_fdr$FDR_p.adj)


print(comparison_table)
```

```{r}

  data = subset(games_all, Year %in% c("2023","2022"))

)

  data = subset(games_all, Year %in% c("2023","2022"))
)
```
